apps which record the intensity of an audio signal. An app (WaveEditor TM here) displays the audio signal
in the form of a wave, whose amplitude is proportional to the loudness of the audio signal.

field, both place their smartphones at a distance d from each other as shown in the figure. They stand

22. A pulse of sound is generated at the centre of a room of rectangular cross section having
dimensions 20 m × 20 m × 30 m. Speed of sound is 350 m/s. Consider all possibilities of
hearing echoes of this pulse. Some of the instances of time when echoes can be detected at the location of the source are … A. 81 ms HBCSE B. 86 ms C. 96 ms D. 103 ms 7

[INJSO 2017 — question paper]
16. A sound wave of fixed frequency is going through a medium in the X direction. Ignore the velocities of
the particles due to thermal motion and assume that the layers of the medium perform simple
harmonic motions about their mean positions. Graph in the figure represents displacements of the
particles from their mean positions (plotted on Y axis) at a particular instant of time. Some of the
particles are labeled by alphabets a – s. Velocity of the particle G is directed negative at that instant.
Points C, I and O correspond to maximum displacement at that instant.

items.stem: Which of the following is the source of sound?
What does the passage say about the production of sound?
If a tuning fork is struck and brought near a water surface, what observation can be made?
A tuning fork is struck and placed near a water surface. Waves are formed on the surface. What does this observation indicate?
Which of the following best describes how sound reaches the ear?
What does the vacuum bell jar experiment show about sound propagation?
In the slinky experiment, what does the mark on the slinky represent?
A student places a tuning fork on a table and strikes it. The tuning fork vibrates and produces sound. What will happen if the tuning fork is placed in a vacuum?
Based on the description of the slinky experiment, which of the following best describes how sound travels through a medium?
A sound wave is generated in a room with dimensions 10 m × 10 m × 20 m. The speed of sound is 350 m/s. How long does it take for an echo to be heard from the farthest wall?
Which of the following best explains why astronauts in space cannot hear each other directly?

A student conducts an experiment in an open field by placing two smartphones at a distance d from each other. They clap one after another, and the sound is recorded by an app that displays the audio signal as a wave. What can be said about the frequency of the sound wave recorded on the smartphones?
Based on the diagram in the passage showing the movement of grains due to sound, what can be concluded about the nature of sound waves?

A sound pulse is generated at the center of a rectangular room with dimensions 20 m × 20 m × 30 m. The speed of sound is 350 m/s. Which of the following times could be the time at which an echo is heard at the source?
What is the main thing that travels through a medium when a sound wave is produced?
What type of wave is a sound wave?
When a piston in a tube is oscillating, what kind of disturbances are produced in the air inside the tube?
In the graph shown in Fig. 10.16b, what does the horizontal dashed line represent?
What is the primary factor that determines the intensity of a sound wave?
If a sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz, what is the time period of the wave?
A sound wave travels through a medium. At a certain instant, the displacement of a particle from its mean position is maximum. What is the direction of the velocity of this particle at that instant?
The graph in Fig. 10.33 represents two sound waves propagating at the same speed. What can be said about their wavelengths?
A sound wave is produced in a room with dimensions 20 m × 20 m × 30 m. The speed of sound is 350 m s. Which of the following times could be when an echo is heard at the source?
Which of the following is an example of a sound wave's characteristic?

Two identical sound sources are placed at A and B — one in air and one submerged in water. The time taken by the sound to return to A is 4.5 times that of B. What is the ratio between the speeds of sound in air and water?
If a sound is heard as an echo after 0.5 seconds, what is the distance to the reflecting surface?
What is the main reason echoes are not heard in small rooms?
A sonar signal is sent into seawater and returns after 0.90 s. If the speed of sound in seawater is 1530 m/s, what is the distance to the object?
What is the minimum distance for an echo to be heard if the speed of sound is 343 m/s?

A student uses a mobile app to generate a sound wave with a frequency of 100 Hz. She then increases the frequency in steps of 100 Hz up to 1000 Hz and listens to the changes. What change in the sound would she most likely notice as the frequency increases?
What is the term used to describe how humans perceive the frequency of a sound wave?

Two friends are standing 340 m apart along a steel fence. One friend knocks the fence, and the other listens. The speed of sound in air is 340 m/s and in steel is 5100 m/s. What is the time difference between the sound reaching the listener through air and through steel?
A person standing near a large building claps their hands, and an echo is heard 2 seconds later. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, what is the minimum distance of the building from the person?
What is the relationship between the amplitude of a sound wave and the energy it carries?
What is transferred when a sound wave travels through a medium?

A sound wave with a frequency of 200 Hz is produced in a room. A person standing in the room hears the sound, and the sound wave reflects off the walls, creating an echo. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s and the time delay between the original sound and the echo is 0.5 seconds, what is the minimum distance of the reflecting surface from the source?
A sound wave is represented on a graph, and the wavelength is found to be 50 meters. If the speed of sound in steel is 5000 m/s, what is the frequency of the sound wave?
What is the unit of frequency of a sound wave?
What is the definition of the amplitude of a sound wave?
If the frequency of a sound wave is increased, what happens to the number of compressions passing a point in a given time?
A sound wave is produced in a medium. How do the particles of the medium behave as the wave travels through it?
In a large hall, sound persists after the source stops due to multiple reflections. What is this phenomenon called?
